inputs.text: ABU DHABI, 16th February, 2026 (WAM) -- The National Centre of Meteorology (NCM) warned today of active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds, raising dust and sand and reducing horizontal visibility to less than 3,000 metres in some coastal and inland areas. The Centre stated in a statement issued today that the weather conditions began at 10:30 and will continue until 18:00, urging the public to exercise caution, particularly when driving on external and open roads, due to the risk of sudden drops in visibility caused by blowing dust.

requested_area.areaDesc: Coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone)

fields.description: EXERCISE - Active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds are raising dust and sand, cutting visibility to under 3,000 m in some coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi (demo zone). Conditions until 18:00.
fields.headline: EXERCISE: Blowing dust reducing visibility in coastal and inland areas until 18:00
fields.instruction: Take care, especially when driving on external and open roads, as visibility can drop suddenly. More information: https://alerts.example.ae
left_out: No unverified inputs were provided, so nothing was excluded.
The start time (10:30) was left out of the phone text to keep it short; the end time (18:00) is included.
fields.note_for_reviewer: This is based on the NCM statement for 16 February 2026. The source does not give a time zone, so I assumed local time for 18:00. Severity is set to Moderate because visibility is under 3,000 m, not near zero; please confirm the demo zone matches the NCM's 'some coastal and inland areas' wording.

This is acceptable as a labelled exercise demo zone, but a live alert would need the area taken from the bulletin, not the dateline.

payload.summary: The alert matches the verified NCM bulletin. It covers the same hazard (northwesterly winds raising dust and sand), the same visibility threshold (under 3,000 m), the same coastal and inland areas and the same end time (18:00). Observed certainty and Immediate urgency fit conditions that began at 10:30 and are ongoing. Moderate severity does not overstate a caution-level warning. No unverified report is used.

no_basis.concern: The console environment is 'live' and the scope is 'Public' for an Exercise-status alert. Approvers should confirm that the drill is meant to reach the public through the live system, presumably on the UAE exercise cell-broadcast channel, rather than a test or limited distribution. The status itself correctly stays 'Exercise'.
no_basis.searched_for: A clause requiring exercise-status alerts to use a non-public scope, or forbidding them on a live console.

objections.fix: Add a short protective action to both languages and put it at the very start, right after 'EXERCISE -' / 'تمرين -'. For example: 'Dust storm: drive with caution, reduce speed; people with breathing conditions stay indoors.' This puts the hazard and the action on page 1. Keep the location and time details after it.
objections.issue: Neither the English nor the Arabic phone text contains a recommended action for recipients. They only describe the hazard (winds raising dust and sand, visibility under 3,000 m) and its duration. The first page therefore cannot carry the action. This matters most in Arabic, where a UCS-2 page holds only about 41 characters (82 octets).

payload.summary: Both required languages (ar, en) are present. Neither exceeds the 15-page maximum (en 3 pages GSM-7, ar 5 pages UCS-2), and the encodings suit the scripts. However, neither language gives recipients any protective action. The text describes the dust hazard and its duration only, so the first page cannot carry the action. The drafter can fix this.

payload.summary: I compared the Arabic headline, description and instruction with the English and found no difference in meaning. The EXERCISE label (تمرين) appears in both the headline and the description. The hazard is the same: blowing dust and sand raised by active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds. The visibility figure (under 3,000 m), the area (some coastal and inland areas, Abu Dhabi demo zone) and the end time (18:00) all match. The protective action also matches: take care, especially when driving on external and open roads, because visibility can drop suddenly. The URL is identical. The Arabic was produced by machine translation, so a named person who reads Arabic must still review and approve it before release.

left_out: Reviewer's example action 'reduce speed' was not used as worded. NCM only urges caution when driving on external and open roads, so the action is limited to that.
Reviewer's example action 'people with breathing conditions stay indoors' was left out. No verified input mentions health advice.
Reviewer's example term 'Dust storm' was not used. NCM describes winds raising dust and sand, not a dust storm, so 'Blowing dust' is used instead.
Arabic phone text was not produced. This task asks for one English alert, so the Arabic version must be fixed separately with the same verified action wording.
fields.note_for_reviewer: The protective action now opens the phone text right after 'EXERCISE -', as the reviewer asked, but it uses only NCM's verified advice (caution on external/open roads). Please confirm that tying NCM's 'some coastal and inland areas' to the operator-chosen Abu Dhabi demo zone is acceptable.

Approvers may still want to confirm that distribution maps to the Exercise cell broadcast channel and not a public warning channel.

Both are well under the 15-page cell broadcast maximum, and the page counts match the character counts. The first page of each language carries the hazard (blowing dust) and the action (drive with caution); in Arabic, 41 UCS-2 characters a page still covers 'غبار متطاير: يرجى القيادة بحذر'. Length within the limit is already recorded under G6.
